from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Can blocks colliding count the digits of Pi?",
            "Two blocks bounce on a frictionless surface.",
            "Small Block A sits near a wall.",
            "Larger Block B blocks the path.",
            "Total collisions reveal the digits of Pi."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Hook: The Bouncing Block Paradox", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets
        wall = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/wall.svg", color="#4D4D4D")
        block_a = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg", color=WHITE)
        block_b = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg", color=WHITE)
        
        # Positions
        self.place_at_grid(wall, 'B3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(block_a, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(block_b, 'C5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.add(wall, block_a, block_b)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        self.play(block_a.animate.shift(RIGHT*0.5), block_b.animate.shift(LEFT*0.5), run_time=1)
        # Bounce simulation (change color to #FF5733 at peak)
        self.play(block_a.animate.set_color("#FF5733"), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.play(block_a.animate.set_color("#33FF57"), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#3357FF"))
        self.play(block_b.animate.set_color("#3357FF"), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF33F6"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Deep Dive: The 1:100 Ratio", [
            "Increase mass ratio by powers of 100.",
            "Total collisions match consecutive digits of Pi.",
            "1:100 ratio yields 31 collisions."
        ])
        
        # Assets
        block_a = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg", color="#2ECC71")
        block_b = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg", color="#3498DB")
        ratio_label = Text("1 : 100", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1: Increase mass ratio by powers of 100. ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Using grid cells 4-6 per B004
        self.place_at_grid(block_a, 'B4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(block_b, 'B6', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.add(block_a, block_b)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2: Total collisions match consecutive digits of Pi. ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Shrinking block_b
        target_b = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg", color="#3498DB")
        self.place_at_grid(target_b, 'B6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(Transform(block_b, target_b))
        
        # Highlight 1:100
        self.place_at_grid(ratio_label, 'C4', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(FadeIn(ratio_label))
        self.play(Indicate(ratio_label, color="#F1C40F"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3: 1:100 ratio yields 31 collisions. ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Scaling demonstration
        for _ in range(3):
            self.play(block_a.animate.scale(1.2), run_time=0.2)
            self.play(block_a.animate.scale(1/1.2), run_time=0.2)
        
        # Visual representation of 31 collisions
        collision_counter = VGroup(*[Dot(color=RED, radius=0.05) for _ in range(5)])
        self.place_in_area(collision_counter, 'E3', 'E5', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(collision_counter))
        
        # Final cleanup
        self.play(FadeOut(block_a), FadeOut(block_b), FadeOut(ratio_label), FadeOut(collision_counter))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis & Summary", [
            "Mechanical systems produce transcendental constants.",
            "Conservation laws create geometric shadows of Pi.",
            "Discrete impacts mirror continuous mathematical truth."
        ])
        
        gear = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/gear.svg")
        pendulum = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pendulum.svg")

        shadow = Circle(radius=1.5, color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=4)

            Square(side_length=0.5, color="#FF69B4", fill_opacity=0.5),

outline.topic: The Curious Link: Block Collisions and the Digits of Pi

sections.title: The Hook: The Bouncing Block Paradox
sections.content: Introduce the physical system: two blocks of different masses on a frictionless surface, with a wall on the left. Block A (mass m) sits between the wall and Block B (mass M). We count the number of collisions.
sections.example: A small ant (Block A) and a large elephant (Block B) sliding on ice towards a solid stone wall.

sections.title: Prerequisites: Conservation Laws
sections.content: Briefly explain that in elastic collisions, both Kinetic Energy and Momentum are conserved. Use a vector diagram to show how velocity vectors change after impact, emphasizing the velocity reflection rule.
sections.example: Visualizing the velocity vectors of the ant and elephant as arrows changing direction upon collision, represented by a reflection across an energy-conserving boundary.

sections.title: The Scaling Connection: Phase Space
sections.content: Explain that the collision system can be mapped to a billiard ball bouncing inside a circular boundary. The 'angle' of the collision represents the digits of Pi. As mass M increases by powers of 100, the collision count increases by digits of Pi.
sections.example: An animation showing a light ray bouncing inside a circle; as the mass ratio M/m grows, the 'path' of the collision count converges to 3.1415...

sections.title: Deep Dive: The 1:100 Ratio
sections.content: Demonstrate that if Block B is 100^n times heavier than Block A, the total number of collisions is exactly the first n+1 digits of Pi.
sections.example: Table graphic: 1:1 ratio = 3 collisions; 1:100 ratio = 31 collisions; 1:10,000 ratio = 314 collisions.

sections.title: Synthesis & Summary
sections.content: Summarize how a mechanical, discrete system (blocks hitting) generates a transcendental, continuous constant (Pi). Reiterate that the physics of conservation laws creates a geometric shadow of Pi.
sections.example: Final visual: A computer simulation of blocks colliding, where the collision counter progressively spells out 3.14159...
